newsitem.title: INDIA: India edible oil steady, arrivals restricted.
newsitem.headline: India edible oil steady, arrivals restricted.

text.p: Indian edible oil prices were steady in domestic markets despite restricted arrivals of the summer oilseeds crop on account of public holidays, industry officials and traders said on Wednesday.
"The market is absolutely steady," Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
But he expected arrivals to rise from next week. "Crop arrivals will pick up from next week," Shah said.

Traders said groundnut oil was quoted at 36,000 rupees per tonne, the same as last week. Palm olein oil was traded at 28,600 rupees compared with 28,500 rupees last week. Soy oil was quoted at 28,300 rupees in local markets.
"Nearly 20 percent of the summer crop has been harvested," Shah said. "Imports have slowed down due to new arrivals."
The Agriculture Ministry expects the summer oilseeds output to rise to 9.92 million tonnes from 9.7 million last year.
